title: uint32
summary: Convert values to unsigned 32-bit integer class.

gpu_support.notes: Real gpuArray inputs use the provider's native integer-cast operation and return resident uint32 storage.

description: `uint32(X)` converts numeric, logical, character, symbolic-constant, and real gpuArray inputs to unsigned 32-bit integer values using saturating rounded conversion.
behaviors: Rounds fractional numeric values to the nearest integer.
Converts all eight integer classes directly from native storage without a floating-point intermediate.
Preserves array shape. A complex host input remains complex when its converted imaginary component is zero.
Real gpuArray inputs return provider-owned native uint32 storage; complex gpuArray conversion requires provider support for paired complex-integer storage.

faqs.question: Does `uint32` preserve array shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. Non-scalar array inputs keep their original dimensions and are tagged with the `uint32` numeric class.

gpu_residency: Real gpuArray inputs remain resident and return native uint32 storage owned by the same provider.
gpu_behavior: The active provider performs real integer conversion through its native cast hook.
Complex gpuArray conversion is unavailable until the provider interface supports paired complex-integer storage.
